arxiv:2608.13167.rationale: While the paper addresses a real production concern (model hallucination and calibration), it focuses on VLM perception gaps rather than RAG/agentic/document intelligence systems, and the findings (output steering via representation manipulation) are interesting but not actionable for practitioners building retrieval or orchestration systems in the 6-month horizon.

arxiv:2608.14626.rationale: This is a systematic literature review on a safety/alignment topic with limited immediate production applicability to RAG, agentic systems, document intelligence, or inference optimization—the core domains of applied LLM engineering.

arxiv:2608.14792.rationale: While methodologically rigorous, this is a domain-specific clinical evaluation study with limited transferable insights for production NLP/RAG systems; the leakage control lessons are valuable but the core contribution (SDM detection in pediatric encounters) is outside my applied AI engineering focus areas.

arxiv:2608.15869.rationale: While this addresses video reasoning with MLLMs, it focuses on visual prediction and world modeling rather than the NLP/RAG/agentic systems core to production document intelligence work; the latency gains are specific to video CoT inference overhead, not generalizable to retrieval-augmented or document-based workflows.

arxiv:2608.20318.rationale: While the benchmark itself is rigorous, the paper focuses on theoretical capability measurement (recursive self-improvement) rather than practical patterns, architectures, or production techniques applicable to current RAG/agentic systems; the finding that LLMs rarely modify training algorithms is observational rather than prescriptive for engineering work.

arxiv:2608.29715.rationale: HD-RoPE directly impacts production inference efficiency and long-context performance—critical for RAG systems and agentic workflows where context length and latency are bottlenecks; the engineering-friendly design without additional parameters makes it immediately applicable to model serving and fine-tuning pipelines.

arxiv:2609.00064.rationale: This is a mechanistic interpretability paper analyzing attention patterns during fine-tuning—theoretically interesting but lacks actionable guidance for production RAG, agentic systems, or document intelligence pipelines, and the Goodhart failure it describes doesn't map to engineering decisions I'd make in deployed systems.
